what: Scope is a re-arrangement, not a build
why: ~60 closed tickets already landed the islands, the Miller picker, the drag ghost and the map-as-background; rebuilding them would be the expensive mistake
evidence: 3 explorer reports over src/, git log showing feat/islands-wizard, feat/fleet-picker, feat/setup-layout all merged into main
result: Scope set to re-arrange the existing console and add the missing domain capabilities

what: The five game states are real, and four already exist
why: planning/preparation/execution/closure are Minos values, and main.rs already projects them via users_project_stage
result: GameState enum adopted as the single driver of the side zone

what: dynamic is prose, not a wire value
why: The backend's own comment equates the concept's "dynamic" with the constant GameModeManeuver; a test lists "dynamic" as invalid
result: Client binds labels to wire values maneuver/static/scenario and never sends "dynamic"

what: static refuses ordering, so an Orders island must hide in it
why: AllowsSteering is false for static only, and the order route 409s
result: Zone contents became a function of state AND mode, not state alone

what: The scenario composer has a real backend
why: There is a per-game book of ordered scenarios, each with ordered steps, plus a per-step assumed-clock window
result: Composer scoped to the book, not to a global catalog

what: A step has no title
why: The backend states the content IS the label, by decision
result: Composer renders content-only rows, no title field

what: Personnel cannot read the book
why: read is granted to judge side and Game Master only; the router calls the book what the exercised must not see
result: Composer is staff-only and hides itself from a Commando seat

what: /users/me carries everything the user island needs
why: email, name, photo_url and full app roles with ids and names all arrive; the current client parses only id and role ids
result: Blocker 5 resolved: avatar is photo_url with a default person glyph, and role names are readable

what: No positive "this role needs a fleet" flag exists
why: Searched for requires_unit/needs_assignment/is_commander: zero matches; the only role flag is is_judge_side, which is the inverse
result: Player Picker derives assignment need from is_judge_side and the one-command rule, and says so on the face

what: The side zone must float over the map, not sit beside it
why: The operator's subject is the map; a dock that resizes it reflows what they are reading
evidence: Design decision, stated in DESIGN.md "Map stage"
result: egui Panel dropped for the side zone; Area on Order::Middle above the map

what: Overlay docking moves the visible map centre
why: CentralPanel keeps full-window size under a floating zone, so a centred unit would park under the chrome
evidence: Derived from chrome.rs:300 already being interactable on Order::Middle
result: Rule added: camera goals offset by half the zone width toward the open side

what: Register: tactical with heat, chosen over diegetic console
why: Glow is the one thing that survives a dim field panel in daylight, and the heat budget can be spent on attention rather than on chrome
evidence: User's decision, after both alternatives were argued
result: One accent, reserved; heat confined to rim and band

what: Every island's rim lit in cyan fails
why: Rendered with two islands up, the accent was on every surface and "cyan" stopped decoding as anything
result: Rim is Cut Grey at rest, Radar Cyan only on the island that owns input

what: Vent slots rejected
why: 40 slots at 3px on an 8px pitch is a dashed rule, and a dashed rule through the title reads as a rendering fault
result: Vent pass deleted; not carried into DESIGN.md

what: Scanlines across the body rejected
why: Rules cut through the rows and the smallest text on the panel (the class line under each hull name) lost legibility first
result: Scanline confined to the title band at 4px/17-255, confirmed legible in a re-render

what: Texture and hardware detail belong on the band, never a body
why: Both rejected passes failed the same way, so the lesson generalises rather than being two separate rulings
evidence: Derived from the two rejections above
result: Stated as a rule in DESIGN.md "Texture, confined"

what: Island open/close may animate again
why: The old ban existed because the close button was already the feedback; islands now arrive as a column and a 150ms settle is what makes the column read as a stack
evidence: Supersedes the previous DESIGN.md Motion rule
result: 150-200ms cubic_out reinstated for islands and modals

what: Mode toggle moves out of the toolbar
why: Presentation vs Simulation is a startup decision, not an operating control; simulation should not announce itself
result: Top zone carries status, count, clock, logout; mode toggle lives in a settings modal

what: Screenshot capture must verify itself
why: A fixed sleep raced cargo run and produced plausible PNGs of the wrong window twice; a stale window also silently invalidated a hardcoded crop
evidence: /tmp/opencode/shoot.sh, three FAILED probe runs before the compositor-geometry crop
result: Probe samples panel-body pixel, and the crop comes from hyprctl's reported window rectBand texture overflowed its band
column5: The texture's height was a literal 48px against a 30px title band, so 18px of rules landed on the body's first rows
column7: BAND_TEXTURE_H is now tokens::TITLE_H, and the two cannot drift apart again

what: Band alpha was too strong
why: 17/255 read as a venetian blind across the title rather than as a surface finish
result: Dropped to 9/255, which reads as texture

what: Trailing note collided with the close button
why: The band ends at right-CUT and the button sits at right-CLOSE_INSET, so a note placed at the band's own edge lands under the button
result: Note is right-aligned against the button's left edge, not the band's

what: Rim ownership resolved centrally rather than per island
why: If each island asked its own hovered, two overlapping islands would both light and the accent would mean nothing; ADR-0016's claim was unenforceable as written
evidence: chrome::owning_island, and a test sweeping ~78k points over the column asserting no point is claimed twice
result: island_owned takes ownership as a parameter; island() keeps the self-contained path so main.rs's six call sites still compile

what: Camera correction sampled the shift instead of the target pixel
why: visible_center passed the pixel shift to unproject_mercator, which takes a viewport-relative pixel, so the centre moved the wrong way by the map's own width
evidence: cargo test --lib a_left_covered_zone, which failed on the first run and caught it
result: Now samples w/2 + shift; two tests assert the old centre renders at w/2 - shift, which is the same statement as content moving toward the open side

what: Advance and close verbs re-homed into the zone
why: Deleting the phase bar and the setup wizard removed the only call sites of setup_advance_execution and close_game, which is a silent regression rather than a cleanup
evidence: cargo check warnings naming both methods as never used
result: Enter execution moved to the Readiness island, "End session" to the Exercise island, the checklist and "Enter preparation" to the foot of Players

what: Legacy free-floating islands suppressed while the zone holds the left edge
why: They park at x=8, directly under a left-docked zone, so two panels rendered on top of each other
evidence: Run and screenshot: the Login island was visible behind the New session island
result: zone_owns_left_edge gates Login, Log, Messages and Roster; they stay for Presentation, which has no zone

what: SimStage, sim_stage, sim_phase_bar and PHASE_BAR_TOP deleted
why: GameState plus the zone's trailing note carry what they carried, and keeping a second axis over the same fact is how the layout ended up spread across three surfaces
evidence: cargo check warnings went from 6 new to 0
result: wizard and phase bar removed; setup_step_lock survives as the per-island picker note

what: AuthenticatedUser carries the whole /users/me projection
why: Only id and app_role_ids were parsed, so the Operator island had to print APP ROLE 1 and a glyph; the backend returns name, email, photo_url and role names in the same response
evidence: Run and screenshot: superuser@tfg.domain shown, APP ROLE 1 replaced by Administrator
result: AppRole {id, name} replaces Vec<i64>; auth_app_role_ids deleted, auth_identity added, LoginDone carries one object instead of two slices

what: Capability asks by role id, display asks by role name
why: A role row may be renamed in the CMS without revoking its policies, so a name comparison would change what the UI allows when someone renames it
result: MinosAuth::has_app_role(id) for capability, app_role_label() for the island tag

what: A role row with no id is dropped, not defaulted
why: It cannot answer a capability question, and an invented id would grant whatever it collided with
result: Skipped in parse_user; a row with a name but no id contributes nothing

what: parse_user extracted from me() so it is testable
why: My first version of the test re-implemented the parser inline and drifted from it, which is the failure a test that mirrors code cannot catch
evidence: cargo test --lib backend::tests, first run failed on label() returning empty
result: pure fn parse_user(&Value), three tests over the cases the contract allows

what: The top zone is an Area, not a Panel
why: A Panel takes space from the CentralPanel, which is what DESIGN.md forbids; the side zone made the same argument and the band had to be consistent with it
evidence: cargo check, then a run at 960 points wide
result: One row: link, headcount, next action, zoom, clock, settings, sign-out right

what: Mode toggle moved out of the toolbar into the settings modal
why: Presentation versus Simulation is a startup decision, not an operating control, and Simulation does not announce itself
result: Settings owns mode, layout preferences, text size and reduced motion

what: Grid, zone visibility and dock edge moved from the band into Settings
why: They are layout preferences that do not change mid-exercise, and carrying them in the band is what made the right-hand group collide with the left one at a narrow width
evidence: Screenshot at 960 points after the move: one clean row
result: Top zone carries only link, headcount, hint, zoom, clock, Settings, sign-out

what: LinkState is a type beside live_status
why: The message is a human sentence and the state is not; classifying the sentence at every read would put a substring match on every frame of a console whose rule is that state says its own colour
evidence: cargo check, enum with label() and ink()
result: Five variants, each with its own status ink, set at the five sites that already set the message

what: Participant carries joined_at
why: The top zone's headcount has to distinguish seated from in-the-room, and the server already returns joined_at; without it "how many are online" could only have been the roster length, which is a different number
evidence: cargo check, field added and parsed
result: Headcount reads "in room / seated", and Presentation shows no headcount rather than a zero that reads as failure

what: Reduced motion is now wired
why: DESIGN.md promised a single switch and nothing implemented it; the zone and the band both animate, so the promise was load-bearing
evidence: ui() writes style.animation_time from one motion_secs constant
result: motion_secs 0.2 normally, 0 under reduced motion

what: Modals are their own chrome primitive, not ad-hoc egui::Window
why: A modal has two obligations its callers all got wrong or would forget: a drag that starts in a form and ends outside it must not reach the map, and it must paint above the zones. Both belong in one place
evidence: chrome::modal, with the backdrop as a real Sense::click_and_drag widget painted before the panel
result: Order::Foreground (egui 0.36 has no Order::Top), full-viewport backdrop first, then the panel

what: A modal is clamped to the window, never reflowed
why: A modal that shrinks to fit a small screen reflows a form the operator is halfway through, and a form whose fields move under the cursor is worse than one with a scrollbar
result: rect_in clamps width and height to the viewport

what: The modal body rect is clamped to non-negative
why: The naive top-left/bottom-right subtraction yields a NEGATIVE height on a window shorter than the title row plus both pads, and scope_builder handed a negative rect lays content out somewhere other than inside the panel
evidence: chrome::tests::the_body_survives_a_tiny_window failed on the first run, twice: once because the fix used Rect::min_size which does not exist, once because from_min_max does not sort its corners
result: Both corners are now sorted explicitly with min/max per axis

what: Modals are square, not chamfered
why: The chamfer means "this whole surface moves" (ADR-0014) and a modal does not move; a chamfered modal would promise a drag that does not exist
result: painted with CornerRadius::ZERO and a hairline, in the third zone

what: The composer authors a game's OWN book; it is not a picker over a catalog
why: A game has exactly one book and the book IS its ordered scenarios - no books table, no cross-game template - so a "choose a scenario from elsewhere" affordance would have no source to choose from
result: Left column is this game's scenarios, right column is the open scenario's steps

what: The composer's modal is openable with an EMPTY book
why: The add-scenario field lives inside the modal, so a modal that required a selected scenario would have no reachable path to the only way to get one
result: A separate visibility flag rather than `composer_scenario.is_some()`

what: A step is a draft until the server names it
why: The backend assigns ids and every write answers with the WHOLE scenario, so writing straight through would blank the form and lose the cursor mid-sentence
result: ComposerDraft + add_scenario_step clears only on a valid draft

what: Half a window is refused in the client
why: The backend refuses a start without an end (or the reverse), but that refusal arrives after the author finished typing rather than while they are in the field
result: ComposerDraft::problem, checked before spawn_rest

what: A nested step takes its scenario_id from its PARENT
why: Reading it from the child meant a step was silently dropped for omitting a field it did not need, losing a row from the list with nothing on screen to explain it
evidence: main tests::a_step_takes_its_scenario_from_the_parent failed with 0 of 1 steps on the first run
result: parse_scenario_step(step, parent_id); only `id` is required of the child

what: A book write SPLICES its scenario into the local list
why: The write answers with ONE scenario; replacing the list with it would drop every other scenario the author was not currently looking at
result: One slot, two shapes; `One` merges by id

what: HHMM is validated exactly as strictly as the server parses it
why: The server's parser takes exactly four digits, hour<=23, minute<=59; a looser client check turns an immediate local correction into a 400 from the field
result: hhmm_ok / hhmm_window_ok, one rule shared by draft and client

what: Holding another game clears the book
why: The book belongs to a game, so a stale book would show the previous session's scenarios and a write against them would be refused by a boundary invisible on screen
result: clear alongside users_game_state

what: The composer button is ABSENT outside planning, not greyed
why: Authoring is a planning-time act and the server refuses it after, so a control that would 403 is a lie about what this session can do
result: Rendered only when users_game_state == "planning"

what: A modal's backdrop gains a CLEAR variant
why: Two of the backdrop's jobs are independent: swallow input, and darken what is behind. A picker drag starts inside the panel and ends on the map, and the drag ghost is painted BY the map, so under a dim it is the dimmest thing on screen exactly when its legibility matters most
result: Backdrop::Clear skips the fill; the Sense::click_and_drag allocation is unconditional

what: A release over the picker panel is not a drop
why: The map is full-bleed under the floating zones, so its rect CONTAINS the modal; "released over the map" alone would place a hull at whatever sea lies behind the form
result: The panel rect is published per frame from the same Modal::rect_in the primitive used, and excluded in drop_lands_on_map

what: The panel rect is published even on the frame the modal closes
why: The drop runs later in the same frame, on the release that closed the modal, and on that frame the panel is still where the pointer left it
result: fleet_panel_rect is cleared when the picker is closed, not when it closes

what: The drop-refusal rule is a free function
why: The rule is pure and the app is not; a rule only checkable by standing up a store, a core map and a token is a rule that does not get checked
result: Called with `self.fleet_panel_rect` at the one call site

what: The Fleet island shows the RESULT, the modal holds the register
why: The four Miller columns are a means, not a summary; in a 320-point zone column they would be the only thing on the island
result: Island shows a "Fleet picker (N assigned)" button and the pieces list

what: A refused drop says WHICH refusal
why: release over the map for a release that was over the form asks the operator to fix something that was not the problem
result: two distinct status strings, chosen by whether the point is in the panel

what: The Player Picker is ONE form, not three surfaces
why: Seating is one decision about a person — who, as what game role, and for some roles which fleet. Split across three surfaces a role ends up seated with no command, and nobody notices until the exercise starts
result: Directory left, roster editor right, one modal

what: The Players island's roster is READ ONLY
why: The editable roster is in the modal and both are on screen at once while it is open. egui keys a widget by Id, so two ComboBoxes salted ("roster-role", user_id) in one frame are ONE widget: one popup, opened from the wrong copy, with clicks landing in the other
result: users_roster_ui split from roster_editor_ui; the island copy carries no ComboBox and no verbs

what: May need a command is derived from is_judge_side
why: There is no positive requires-a-fleet flag on a game role — the helpers mirror carries is_judge_side and nothing else — so the honest question is "is this the judge side" and the answer for the rest is a WARNING, not a block
result: Amber "no command yet" on the roster row, grey note under the seat-as combo

what: The "may need a command" note appears BEFORE the seat is taken
why: A commander with no fleet is otherwise discovered when the exercise starts, which is the worst possible moment
result: One line under the combo; costs nothing and can be ignored

what: A release over a form says so, before the "no marker there" advice
why: The map's rect CONTAINS the panel, so the marker arm would answer "release over a unit marker" — advice about a place the operator was never aiming at
result: in the user-drag arm, the panel check is the FIRST arm

what: Panel rects are a Vec cleared once per frame
why: Two modals each own a drag-to-map. A single slot would mean whichever drew last silently disarmed the other, and a panel cannot remove its own rect on the frame it closes — which is exactly the frame where a release lands
result: modal_panel_rects, cleared before any panel draws

what: The whole GameDetail is kept, not cherry-picked
why: parse_game_detail dropped six of the game's fields, so `description` was WRITE-ONLY: the form sent it and nothing read it back. The same defect bit parse_user, four of five fields. Keeping the response whole makes the next unparsed field a visible omission
result: Six prose/three-state/end fields parsed; 5 tests

what: A three-state field is read as an ABSENCE, empty prose as an empty string
why: `area`/`map_tag`/`overlay_text` are omitted when unset AND (for area) when withheld, so an empty string must not become a value; `description`/`purpose`/`target` are always sent, so absent means unwritten
result: Two different reads for two different wire shapes, not one helper for both

what: An absent area is withheld only from a PARTICIPANT before execution
why: The two absences are the same shape on the wire, so the difference is who is asking. A Game Master is never withheld; reading the state alone would tell the person editing the plan that their own area is hidden
result: GameDetail::area_is_withheld(is_game_master), taking BOTH facts

what: The plan is read-only on the island
why: The edit form is blank-means-unchanged with empty meaning CLEAR, so seeding its drafts from the detail would make every save clear the two nullable columns
result: The parser fix is what makes the field readable; seeding the drafts would break the write

what: Onboard::Mode is deleted, not deprecated
why: The card asked "Command Center or Tactical Floor Game?" before the map was up, which is the app naming its own function to the person about to use it. A launch reaches Simulation because that is what the console is for; Presentation stays reachable, not offered as a peer
evidence: the brief: Simulation must not announce itself
result: Onboard is Login | App; login goes straight to enter_shell(Simulation); onboard_mode and mode_card_text deleted

what: Settings offers a VIEW, not a peer mode
why: Two buttons named for modes puts them on equal footing as if they were things you choose between. Presentation is a way of watching a session; "Watch only" names what the toggle turns ON, and the line under it says which you are in
result: One toggle, plus a line stating the current view

what: The Execution column is four islands in dependency order
why: Execution is the state the console spends its life in, so the column is a working surface rather than a summary: what time it is (read most), what you can order (the verb), then who is here and what just happened underneath both
result: Exercise, Orders, Crew, Log — 200/420/240/260

what: Closure carries Assessment and Log, and deliberately NO Orders
why: Closure is read-only. An Orders island there would show controls the server refuses, which is a lie about the state
result: Assessment, Log

what: Crew counts IN THE ROOM, not seated
why: `joined_at` is the fact that matters and it is not the roster: a participant is SEATED when given a role and IN THE ROOM when they arrive with the room key. During execution the difference is a commander who can be reached and one assigned to nobody
result: Two marks, plus a not-arrived amber

what: The Orders surface was EXTRACTED, not rewritten
why: 184 lines of jurisdiction and authority checks. Re-deriving any of it while moving it is how a refactor becomes a rewrite
result: The free-floating island now calls it; the column calls it

what: A surface is in the column or floating, never both
why: Two copies of the Orders panel is not two views of one thing — it is the operator editing one and looking at the other. Gated per SURFACE, not on "the zone is showing", because Execution carries Orders/Crew/Log while Planning carries none and Presentation has no column at all
result: orders and log check it; roster deliberately does NOT

what: The floating Roster is NOT suppressed
why: That island lists SHIPS in view; the column's Crew lists PEOPLE in the room. Different questions, both wanted, and the names differ for the same reason — "Roster" beside "Crew" is not two names for one thing
evidence: ShipApp roster island gate left ungated
result: A test that named it would assert a duplication that does not exist

what: The Orders trailing note resolves a group ID to a name
why: Selection::Group holds a group id, not a name. A trailing note reading "Orders · 4" tells the operator nothing about which four
result: group_info, with "(gone)" when the group has been removed

what: Island bodies are CLIPPED to their rect
why: A `max_rect` tells the LAYOUT where to stop; it does not stop the PAINTER. The Operator island was 112pt against content needing more, and the overflow painted over the map and half-occluded under the next island's title band — reading in the screenshot as a label belonging to the island below
evidence: found by rendering the real app; every rect involved was correct, which is why the 4 zone-geometry tests passed and this shipped anyway
result: island_owned: ui.set_clip_rect(content.intersect(ui.max_rect()))

what: Clipping is a mitigation, not a fit
why: Content that does not fit is now lost quietly instead of loudly. side_zone stacks by heights fixed BEFORE anything is drawn, so they cannot be measured from content without running each body twice — and running a body twice double-fires its writes
result: The honest fix is a non-interactive measure pass, which means bodies stop writing on a dry run

what: The Operator island is 140pt, measured
why: 104 and 128 both clipped the Sign out button on a render. The previous 112 carried a status line that has since come off, so the slack read as an empty band
evidence: rendered at 104, 128, 140 and looked at each
result: Identity row + email + button

what: MODAL_BACKDROP_ALPHA 150 -> 104
why: At 150 the map was essentially gone and the zone islands behind read as ghosts, which contradicts the premise that the map is the background and the interface floats above it. 104 keeps the grid, the symbols and the island outlines legible
evidence: rendered at 150 and at 104 in the harness
result: Judged on a near-black synthetic background; the real tile map is BRIGHT and the exact value there is still unverified

what: The harness gains a BRIGHT map-like ground
why: The harness window is transparent, so every capture showed the near-black desktop wallpaper. Judging a BLACK overlay against a BLACK background tells you nothing, and the real tile map is bright — so the backdrop dim had been judged against the wrong thing entirely
evidence: p5-epaint --island --modal --bright; pixel samples of land under the dim
result: 150 -> land srgb(100,101,96), map stops reading as a map; 104 -> srgb(143,143,136), land/sea/grid/coastline/labels all survive

what: The bright ground painted inside the wrong branch
why: The first version went in after the modal's early `return`, so it never ran and the render showed exactly the previous background. A render identical to the last one is the tell, not a failure to run
result: Renders that look unchanged after adding a background are the symptom

what: Island overflow is PUBLISHED, not just clipped
why: Clipping fixed the corruption but turned "corrupts the island below" into "a button quietly vanishes", which reads as a bug in the form. The loud half is a stderr line a developer can act on
result: Verified live: silent at 140pt, exactly one report at 90pt

what: The overflow threshold is one TEXT LINE, not a hair
why: At 0.5pt every island reported, because a layout's min_rect runs ~4pt past the last control for trailing spacing — the Operator island measures 98.4 against 94 and renders with slack. A signal that fires on everything is worse than none, because the first person to see it learns to ignore it
result: The real 112pt overflow ran ~52pt over, so 12pt separates the cases cleanly

what: A false positive is worth chasing rather than shipping
why: The 0.5pt threshold briefly looked like a SECOND bug in the "New session" island at 168pt. It was padding noise — the same 4pt as everywhere else. Fixing the threshold removed the phantom
result: Sized both islands against their real content before believing either

what: The column MEASURES its island heights instead of being told them
why: The overflow detector was already reporting "content needs more"; using it was cheaper than a measure pass. Each island draws at whatever height it is given, publishes what it wanted, and the NEXT frame stacks with that
evidence: the Operator island shipped at 112pt against content needing 140, found by render
result: chrome::island_fitted_height read from the context's temp storage; verified live: 70pt reports once then self-corrects

what: One frame of lag beats running every body twice
why: The zone stacks by heights fixed before anything is drawn, so measuring IN ADVANCE means running every body twice per frame — and every write a body performs fires twice. A frame of lag cannot fire a write twice
result: Declared constant stays as the first frame's height and as the floor

what: The measurement rides the context's TEMP storage, not a HashMap
why: Temp storage is already scoped to one frame. A parallel field on the app would be a second source of truth that can disagree with it, and the Context is where the island already writes
result: The first draft kept a zone_heights HashMap; it was unused and removed

what: The height clamp REFUSES a nonsense measurement
why: A layout can report zero (empty content) or NaN, and NaN through clamp silently poisons a rect, which drops every island under it — so a bad measurement must be worse than no measurement
evidence: main tests::a_nonsense_measurement_is_refused, 5 tests of the clamp
result: fitted_island_height(declared, want, ceiling), pure

what: A uinput pointer is written by hand rather than installed
why: ydotool and dotool both need root; /dev/uinput carries an ACL for this user, so the device can be made directly — which is all either of them does anyway
result: A working pointer after four bare-EINVAL fixes, all recorded in its README

what: The Minos stack runs with no root and no docker
why: Postgres and Valkey are not installed and docker.sock is not accessible, so the Arch packages are fetched and extracted into a local prefix; Postgres then needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH for libnuma
result: Migrated to schema_version 68, API live on :8099, real session created

what: The scenario book needs a GAME MASTER SEAT, not an app role
why: /games/scenarios update is granted to the game role, and the middleware's administrative path needs /system/game-content read, which a stock Administrator does not hold. So authoring scenarios means being in the exercise
result: Seating the account as Game Master made POST /scenarios succeed

what: Casbin's policy set is loaded ONCE, at startup
why: An instance running before the superuser is seeded keeps denying that account, and `pkill -f cmd/minos` does not kill the child binary `go run` built — so the old instance survives and keeps the port. This presents as "the permission is wrong" when it is staleness
result: Killing the real binary and restarting was the fix

what: ONE pointer device must live for a whole interaction
why: Each uim.py call creates and destroys its own device, and focus did not survive the sequence: the second round of clicks and keystrokes went to a different window and typed a password into a chat window. This is why the modal screenshots are still not done
result: Keep one device alive; Mouse is importable for exactly that reason

what: The console could not author a planned window, so no exercise it started could ever reach execution
why: WindowSet is actual_end AND assumed_end non-null, nothing defaults either, and the client had NO write path for any of the four window fields. The button still ENABLED, because the window was not among the checklist blockers, so the operator clicked and got a 409 naming a field the console had no control for
evidence: verified from Minos ReadinessCounts + CanExecute; GameUpdate was six Option<String>
result: TimeWindow on GameUpdate + create/edit forms; the checklist gained the window condition

what: The gate is ONE function and the checklist formats it
why: Three client re-deriations of one server rule have now drifted, and pace was the fourth. The client's copy has only ever agreed with the server on the two counts the server hands it
result: A free six-parameter function over a small input struct, mirroring Minos's own CanExecute test table

what: An unrecognised pace REQUIRES the readiness declaration
why: GamePace::parse returns None for anything this build has not heard of, and None requires the declaration. Guessing the other way starts an exercise while half the players are still reading the brief, and the asymmetry is deliberate
result: GameDetail.pace is Option<GamePace>, fail closed

what: The exercise clock uses ONE fixed base date for both ends
why: validateTimeBase compares each clock only with ITSELF, so the assumed date is free — but if the two ends got different bases, assumed_end > assumed_start would silently break. A window crossing midnight is still refused, and the operator is told rather than the client accepting what the server will reject
